name: Boiled leather armour
description: A suit of thick leather that was boiled and moulded until it set hard: a shaped cuirass, layered shoulder flaps, a skirt of strips and laced guards for the arms and legs. Light for what it stops.
notes: Laid out flat, front up, neck towards -z, 1230 mm long and 840 mm across: a moulded chestnut cuirass with raised chest lobes and a dark stitched edge, three layered flaps at each shoulder, a skirt of eight studded strips, and half-round arm, thigh and shin guards laced up their fronts with tan thongs, with a domed knee cup between thigh and shin. CHECK VOLUME LENGTH: the reference gives the suit packed into a 600 mm bundle; laid out flat its box is longer and emptier. Slot `vest`, as batch 110's cardboard armour and earlier armour batches have it, though the suit also covers the arms and legs; Deadvox has no whole-body armour slot. Protection is a judgement for hardened leather: fair against cuts and blows, weaker against points. The worn look is pending: no worn model is authored.

name: Heavy hardened steel plate armour
description: A heavy suit of hardened steel plate with a thick breastplate and a second plate riveted over the belly, broad pauldrons and full guards for the arms and legs. Almost nothing gets through, and every step shows it.
notes: Laid out flat, front up, neck towards -z, about 1250 mm from the shoulder straps to the ankle and 840 mm across: a curved breastplate with a middle ridge and rolled neck and arm edges, four fauld lames and a mail skirt below it, domed pauldrons, and on each side an arm harness (upper guard, elbow cop with its fan, mail at the elbow, forearm guard) and below a leg harness (thigh guard, knee cop with its wing, mail behind the knee, greave), all strapped in black leather. CHECK VOLUME LENGTH: the reference gives the suit packed into a 600 mm bundle; laid out flat its box is far longer and emptier. The plackart riveted over the lower breastplate, four lames and broad pauldrons set it apart. Plate in `steel-hardened`. Slot `vest`, as batch 110's cardboard armour and earlier armour batches have it, though the suit also covers the arms and legs; Deadvox has no whole-body armour slot. Protection is a judgement for hardened plate over mail: very strong against cuts, strong against points and fair against blows. The xl size shares the model. The worn look is pending: no worn model is authored.

name: Hardened sheet metal armour
description: A full suit hammered out of flat sheet steel and case-hardened: a chest sheet still showing locker vents, hip sheets and bent guards strapped over the arms and legs. Crude, heavy and very hard to bite through.
notes: Laid out flat, front up, neck towards -z, about 1280 mm long and 840 mm across: a shallow chest sheet over a wider back sheet, two banks of louvre vents left from the lockers it was cut from, rows of rivets down each side, two hip sheets, a riveted shoulder sheet on each side, and arm and leg guards bent from flat stock in three facets, buckled on with tan leather straps. Steel in `steel-hardened`; the vents are dark slots under raised slats. The box is close to the reference length, as the reference gives the suit at 1200 mm. Slot `vest`, as batch 110's cardboard armour and earlier armour batches have it, though the suit also covers the arms and legs; Deadvox has no whole-body armour slot. Protection is a judgement for hardened sheet steel: strong against cuts, fair against points and blows. The worn look is pending: no worn model is authored.

name: Chitin armour
description: A cuirass and leg guards built from the shells of giant insects, overlapping like the plates on a beetle's back and laced together with rawhide. Light, stiff and hard to cut.
notes: Laid out flat, front up, neck towards -z, 1120 mm long and 440 mm across: eight overlapping curved shell segments with a raised keel down the middle and rawhide lacing at each side, two rounded shoulder guards over the top corners, and each leg guard a run of eight shell rings that narrow towards the ankle, tied with rawhide. It covers the body and legs, not the arms, as the reference gives. CHECK LENGTH: the reference gives the suit packed into a 600 mm bundle; laid out flat it is longer. Slot `vest`, as batch 110's cardboard armour and earlier armour batches have it, though the suit also covers the legs; Deadvox has no whole-body armour slot. Protection is a judgement for thick insect shell: good against cuts, fair against points and blows, and it shrugs off acid better than metal. The xl and xs sizes share the model. The worn look is pending: no worn model is authored.

name: Fur armour
description: A heavy coat and leggings of layered fur and hide, tied shut with rawhide. It turns a bite or a scrape and keeps out the worst of the cold.
notes: Folded on a shelf, 300 mm by 300 mm and 140 mm tall in four layers: a thick fur coat with its rolled sleeves along both sides, a deep fur collar, a rawhide strip and three pairs of rawhide ties down the front, and shaggy tufts standing up over the top; the leggings are folded inside. Slot `torso`, as the gambesons and other coats have it, though it also covers the arms and legs; Deadvox has no whole-body slot. Protection is a judgement for thick hide and fur: fair against bites and blows, weak against points. The xl and xs sizes share the model. The worn look is pending: no worn model is authored.

name: Rusted plate armour
description: An old suit of fluted plate armour, the kind once kept for show. Its steel is pitted with rust and its straps are cracked and fraying, but it still stops a blade.
notes: Laid out flat, front up, neck towards -z, about 1250 mm from the shoulder straps to the ankle and 840 mm across: a curved breastplate with a middle ridge and rolled neck and arm edges, three fauld lames and a mail skirt below it, domed pauldrons, and on each side an arm harness (upper guard, elbow cop with its fan, mail at the elbow, forearm guard) and below a leg harness (thigh guard, knee cop with its wing, mail behind the knee, greave), all strapped in black leather. CHECK VOLUME LENGTH: the reference gives the suit packed into a 600 mm bundle; laid out flat its box is far longer and emptier. Fluted ridges fan down the breastplate in bright steel over dull iron-grey plate, with rust patches on the chest, an arm and a leg, mail gone rusty red, and frayed tan straps hanging loose off the arm and leg. Low-grade steel reads as `iron-dull`. Slot `vest`, as batch 110's cardboard armour and earlier armour batches have it, though the suit also covers the arms and legs; Deadvox has no whole-body armour slot. Protection is a judgement for thin, corroded mild steel: fair against cuts, weaker against points and blows, and it wears quickly. The worn look is pending: no worn model is authored.
